abstract: A wide range of pathogens continues to threaten bighead carp (Hypophthalmichthys nobilis) aquaculture. Fish cell lines allow host-pathogen interactions to be dissected and candidate control measures to be tested under defined conditions. We established and characterized the first brain-derived cell line from bighead carp, designated HnB, which is only the second cell line reported for this species. HnB cells exhibited stable proliferation in Dulbecco's Modified Eagle Medium (DMEM) containing 5-20% fetal bovine serum (FBS) at 28-32 degrees C and were serially passaged more than 50 times. The species origin of HnB cells was confirmed by PCR amplification and sequencing of the cytochrome b gene, and the sequence obtained showed 100% identity with previously published H. nobilis cytochrome b sequences. The modal chromosome number was 48, and the cells were free of mycoplasma contamination. Transfection with pEGFP-N3 demonstrated that HnB cells support exogenous gene expression. Quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and viral titre assays showed that HnB cells were susceptible to spring viraemia of carp virus (SVCV). Moreover, both interferon alpha (IFN-alpha) and interferon-stimulated gene 15 (ISG15) were significantly up-regulated in HnB cells following exposure to SVCV or poly(I:C), whereas LPS down-regulated the expression of both genes, indicating that HnB cells mount transcriptional antiviral responses to viral and viral-mimetic stimuli. The HnB line therefore supports SVCV replication and gives a species-matched system for studying antiviral (IFN-alpha/ISG15) responses in bighead carp.
